item.title: SRE Goes Left, DevOps Goes Right
item.description: 1. A Process Divorced from Responsibility Is Meaningless Software architecture matches organizational architecture, and this shows up not only in functional boundaries but even more in the division of responsibilities. Only clear responsibility boundaries can build good team collaboration and growth. Every team and every person should understand their own goals — what they should take on and what they should stay out of — and invest their time and energy in things that benefit the primary goal, rather than sinking into trivia.

item.title: When We're on Ticket Duty, What Are We On Duty For?
item.description: 1. When We’re on Ticket Duty, What Are We On Duty For? Most people have probably only ever filed a ticket, never worked one. And people who have worked tickets generally don’t file them lightly. A ticket is a service bundled free with the product a customer paid for, dedicated to solving every kind of usage problem.

item.title: The Software Product Is the Output of Team Capability
item.description: 1. People Matter More and More Why is the valuation of the internet industry significantly higher than that of manufacturing? Among equally excellent companies in their respective industries, Tencent’s PE is as high as 30+, while Gree’s PE is only 10+. The internet industry is characterized by being asset-light: no expensive complex equipment, no need for large production plants.

item.description: 1. About the Service Industry The primary sector, represented by agriculture, solves the problem of survival; the secondary sector, represented by industry, solves the problem of efficiency; the tertiary sector, represented by services, solves other people’s problems. Unless some factor puts people’s physical existence under threat, the service industry has extremely broad room to grow.

item.title: ToB Thinking at Large and Small Companies
item.description: 1. Understanding ToB It is only because money has become harder and harder to make from ToC that ToB has flourished. The era in which a single idea could be turned into a good product and ultimately accepted by everyone has been crushed beneath the wheels. In the early days of the internet, a single portal directory made Sohu, a single chat tool made Tencent, and even hao123 — nothing more than a handful of jump pages — sold for tens of millions.

item.description: The team I am on is responsible for SaaS development. We have a few flagship SaaS products and also some supporting ones. But a flagship project cannot stay the flagship forever — projects have life cycles and phases.

item.title: The R&D Process of Agile Development
item.description: 1. What Agile Development Is In the traditional software development model, the cycle from raising a requirement to final delivery is long. The waterfall model proceeds through six steps: requirements analysis, design, coding, integration, testing, and maintenance. Once a requirement changes, the work invested earlier is not only wasted but also hard to adjust.

item.title: Building a Team with Consistency
item.description: 1. Consistent Understanding In a large organization, we can think of a small team as a microservice. As early as 1967, Conway proposed the concept of the microservice. Conway argued that any organization designing a system will deliver a design whose structure is consistent with that organization’s communication structure. When developing complex systems, we usually split the system into modules.
